writeback.title: Write-back to GitLab
writeback.create: Create an issue from a task
writeback.fetchTemplates: Fetch issue templates from the project
writeback.children: Push subtasks into the GitLab hierarchy
writeback.hint: “Create an issue from a task” adds a “Create a GitLab issue” button to the task modal (under the “Parent” property) — the issue is opened from the task's properties and description under the integration owner's token, after which the task counts as synced. It works independently of the change write-back below. “Fetch issue templates” pulls in {templates} templates — you can pick one above the description editor before creating. “Upload attachments” copies images from the description and comments, plus the task's files, into the GitLab project store — otherwise links to them stay broken inside the issue (GitLab resolves them against its own address). Turn it off if you would rather not duplicate binaries in GitLab: links are then replaced with a note. Deleting a file in Tessera does not remove the GitLab copy — there is no upload-deletion API.
writeback.childrenHint: “Push subtasks” adds a “Mark as grouped” button to the task modal (it sets the label in GitLab), and subtasks of such a parent are created as child items of the issue. The label is set here rather than as a tag: its prefix is owned by a sync rule, which is why the tag picker hides it on purpose — the label has to be read as grouping by this integration's rules, otherwise the server rejects the button. “Label the parent automatically” is off by default: otherwise the very first subtask would quietly edit labels in GitLab; the subtask list shows a hint with a button instead.
